idiom_name: Exposed IntIdTable auto-increment id (or JPA @Id @GeneratedValue in Spring)
implementation_notes: Kotlin reuses the JVM mappers: with JetBrains Exposed the table extends IntIdTable/LongIdTable/UUIDTable and the auto-incrementing id column is created and filled for you (a hand-rolled column is integer("id").autoIncrement().entityId()), while with Spring Data JPA the field carries @Id @GeneratedValue exactly as in Java and the provider assigns the key. The classic key-generator object is replaced by the table class or the annotation plus provider; when the key must exist before the insert, use a UUID table or a clientDefault so the value is set in Kotlin instead of by the database. EntityID<Int> stays nullable until the row exists, which is where the unsaved-state logic belongs.
pitfalls: An IntEntity's id is not a real value until the insert runs: comparing EntityIDs or keying a cache on them before that treats all new entities as one.
Mixing Exposed's DSL with JPA or raw JDBC writes on the same table creates two key-generation paths; pick one per table.

A clientDefault that calls UUID.randomUUID() fixes the key in the application and skips the read-back, while a database default runs server-side: choosing one per column is what decides whether the key exists before the INSERT.
